candidates.title: Capture and qualify incoming leads

demandEvidence.chore: Capture incoming leads and prepare a qualification result for follow-up.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I built a lead capture and qualification workflow in n8n using Apollo, OpenAI, Airtable, Slack, and Gmail.

ease.reason: A small mock can classify operator supplied lead rows, but the post gives no implementation reference or tested setup.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small professional service firms may pay for lead qualification; this build post establishes no buyer or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week test could label synthetic lead rows and prepare follow-up fields; accuracy and integrations remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: A proposed classifier could process rows repeatedly, but a person must verify fit and choose follow-up; no capability reference is supplied.

evidence.reason: The author says they built a lead capture and qualification workflow, but gives no details about demand, results or operation.

candidates.reason: Below threshold: a narrow synthetic lead qualification test is conceivable, but this is a build description rather than clear buyer demand and has no supplied implementation reference.

candidates.title: Draft reminders from spreadsheet due dates

demandEvidence.chore: Check spreadsheet due dates and prepare reminder drafts for review.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I want to connect Google Sheets to my Make scenario using the Search Rows module so I can automate reminders based on due dates stored in a spreadsheet.

ease.reason: A beginner can test supplied date rows and draft reminder text; no supplied building reference supports the Sheets connection.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small professional service firms tracking deadlines may pay for reminder preparation; this request proves no payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week synthetic test can identify due rows and draft reminders; live connection and date edge cases remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: A proposed repeated check could flag dates, but a person must verify them and approve recipients and messages; integration is unsupported.

evidence.reason: The post explicitly names Sheets, due dates and reminders, but gives little frequency or workflow detail.

candidates.reason: Below threshold: the concrete reminder chore can support a synthetic draft test, but no implementation reference supports the connection and evidence is limited.

candidates.title: Triage WhatsApp and email queries

demandEvidence.chore: Sort repeated customer queries across WhatsApp and email and prepare answer drafts.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: We get 50–100 customer queries a day on WhatsApp and email, and want an AI agent to handle most of them.

ease.reason: A sample of fictional queries could be categorized and drafted, but no supplied reference supports messaging integrations or response quality.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: a service team handling recurring customer questions might pay for draft preparation; the request proves no payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week synthetic test can sort examples and prepare drafts; production channels, languages and correctness need review.

autonomy.reason: A proposed loop can categorize and draft, but a person must approve messages and handle uncertain cases; no implementation reference is supplied.

evidence.reason: The request states 50–100 daily queries across two channels and seeks an agent, but supplies no corroboration.

candidates.reason: Reject as duplicate: the specific support-query triage and reply-drafting workflow overlaps recent post 98b4f6281cc3de4ecdfa95f6, regardless of channel or customer label.

rejected.title: Self-host email maintenance
rejected.reason: The discussion says the poster wanted to self-host email and rented a VPS, but identifies no concrete recurring maintenance chore or request for a service; assigning deliverability tasks would invent demand.

rejected.title: Recover a locked workflow account
rejected.reason: This is a one-off access recovery and preservation problem for an existing account, not a repeated workflow suitable for a bounded autonomous service; account recovery also requires sensitive owner access.

rejected.title: Unspecified Make billing problem
rejected.reason: The captured text is only the forum prompt “What is the problem & what have you tried?” and contains no actual chore or issue to assess.

rejected.title: Weekly keyword volume report
rejected.reason: The captured evidence only says the schedule is Monday 9 am UTC and can be changed. It does not identify the requested keyword task, inputs, or report output, so a chore cannot be inferred.

steps.message: Assessed all seven sealed discussion assignments. Three concrete workflow ideas received provisional five-criterion ratings; the support idea duplicates recent support-inbox work. Four assignments lack a specific recurring chore or describe a one-off issue. No eligible nonduplicate idea has enough implementation support to propose.
